title: Protein timing for endurance recovery
chunkText: Consuming 20-40g of protein within 30-60 minutes after endurance exercise supports muscle repair and glycogen replenishment. Plant proteins such as pea-rice blends are complete when combined and are a good choice for dairy-free or vegan athletes.

title: Choosing a low-sugar recovery drink
chunkText: For recovery without excess sugar, look for shakes with under 6g of sugar and at least 20g of protein. High-sugar sports drinks are better suited to mid-race fueling than post-run recovery.

title: When to use electrolyte drinks
chunkText: Electrolyte drinks replace sodium and potassium lost in sweat and are most useful for sessions over 60 minutes or in hot weather. For shorter easy runs, water is usually sufficient.

title: Beginner 5k training basics
chunkText: A typical beginner 5k plan runs 6-8 weeks with 3 runs per week, mixing walk-run intervals that gradually build to continuous running. Rest days and easy pacing prevent injury and build aerobic base.

title: Best running shoes for beginners
chunkText: Beginner runners benefit from a cushioned, stable neutral shoe with a breathable upper. Extra foam under the heel improves comfort during walk-run training, and a lightweight build keeps early runs feeling easy.

title: Road vs trail running shoes
chunkText: Road shoes have smooth or lightly patterned outsoles tuned for pavement, while trail shoes use deep lugs and protective materials for grip and durability on uneven, muddy terrain. Waterproof trail shoes help in wet conditions.

title: Getting the right running shoe fit
chunkText: Leave about a thumb's width between your longest toe and the shoe's end, and shop later in the day when feet are largest. A snug midfoot with a roomy toe box reduces blisters and black toenails on long runs.

title: Caring for waterproof shoes
chunkText: Waterproof membranes work best when the upper is kept clean; rinse off mud and let shoes air-dry away from direct heat. Re-applying a spray-on water repellent restores beading as the finish wears down.

title: Dairy-free protein options
chunkText: Pea, rice, soy and hemp proteins provide complete or complementary amino acid profiles without dairy. They suit lactose-intolerant and vegan athletes and are widely available in ready-to-drink shakes.

title: What to eat before a run
chunkText: Eat a small carbohydrate-focused snack 30-90 minutes before running, keeping fat and fiber low to avoid stomach upset. Energy gels are useful for topping up carbohydrate during runs longer than an hour.
